To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the activity levels of two BBB marker enzymes, gamma-GT and alkaline phosphates, decrease with increasing cell growth, and that the decrease is due to a decrease in the number of enzyme molecules expressed per cell.

cultured cerebral endothelial cell cultures are able to maintain the BBB specific enzymatic properties of gamma-GT and alkaline phosphates, but not the proliferating capacity, for a long period of time.
the activities of the specific BBB marker enzymes gamma-gluta-myltranspept idase and alkaline phosphoatase are lost in proliferating endothelial cells in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the blood-brainer barrier marker enzymes in cultured cerebral endothelia cells.
the question whether the BBB marker enzymes can be used as a marker to identify the BBB in vitro.

a possible correlation between the loss of BBB specific enzymatic activities and the loss of the barrier function in vitro and with the possible use of the BBB specific enzymes gamma-GT, ALP and ACE as marker enzymes for in vitro BBB differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cultured cerebral endothelial cell cultures are a suitable model for the study of the blood-brained barrier.
the BBB marker enzymes are not only expressed by cerebral endothelial cells but are also specifically regulated by the cells.
the loss of gamma-GT and/or ALP in proliferating cerebral endothelial cells is due to a loss of the enzyme molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cultured cerebral endothelial cell lines are a suitable in vitro model for studies on the blood-brain-barrier function, but that they do not express all BBB specific properties.
the BBB marker enzymes are expressed in cerebral endothelial cells and their activity decreases during cell proliferation in culture.

the BBB characteristic enzymatic properties of cultured cerebral endothelial are not only dependent on the presence of structural components of the vascular basement membrane, but also on the proliferative state of the cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of the BBB marker enzyme activities in proliferating endothelial cells in culture is due to a reduced synthesis of the respective enzymes and not to an increased degradation.
the BBB characteristic enzymatic properties are not preserved in cultured cerebral capillary endothelial cell.

in vitro cultured cerebral endothelial cell cultures are a suitable model to study the regulation of BBB marker enzymes and that the observed loss of gamma-GT and alkaline phosphates activities in proliferating cerebral endothelial cells cannot be prevented by the use of structural components of the basement membrane.
